definitions.explanation: A vivid reddish-orange color, traditionally associated with the pigment made from cinnabar. A characteristic color of Japanese shrines and traditional lacquerware.

examples.japanese: {鳥居|とりい}は{朱色|しゅいろ}に{塗|ぬ}られている。
examples.english: The torii gate is painted vermillion.

examples.japanese: {朱色|しゅいろ}の{漆器|しっき}がテーブルに{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Vermillion lacquerware is lined up on the table.

examples.japanese: {秋|あき}になると、{山|やま}の{木々|きぎ}が{朱色|しゅいろ}に{染|そ}まって{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: In autumn, the mountain trees turn vermillion and look beautiful.

notes:
A vivid reddish-orange color with deep roots in Japanese culture. Composed of {朱|しゅ} (vermillion) + {色|いろ} (color). The pigment was originally derived from cinnabar ({辰砂|しんしゃ}), a mercury sulfide mineral.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {朱色|しゅいろ}の{鳥居|とりい}: vermillion torii gate
- {朱色|しゅいろ}に{塗|ぬ}る: to paint vermillion
- {朱色|しゅいろ}に{染|そ}まる: to turn vermillion
- {鮮|あざ}やかな{朱色|しゅいろ}: vivid vermillion

CULTURAL NOTE:
Vermillion is one of the most iconic colors in Japanese culture. Shinto shrine gates ({鳥居|とりい}), temple buildings, and traditional lacquerware frequently feature this color. It is believed to ward off evil spirits and symbolize vitality and prosperity. The {朱|しゅ}{肉|にく} (vermillion ink pad) used for seals ({印鑑|いんかん}) also uses this color.

RELATED WORDS:
- {赤|あか}: red — the most general word for red
- {紅|くれない}: crimson — a deeper, cooler red
- {茜色|あかねいろ}: madder red — a warm red with yellow tones, associated with sunsets
